items.t: Ukraine accuses SpaceX of restricting Starlink, disrupting military as it reels from intel gaps
items.d: Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of disrupting its military operations by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from a pair of intense Russian missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies.
items.fullText: War in Ukraine Ukraine says new Starlink restrictions disrupt military as it reels from intel gaps and Trump clash Ukrainian officials and military units on Wednesday accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of throttling a technology at the heart of their battlefield communications and drone operations. Listen to this article with a free profile 00:00 00:00 A Russian missile hit an apartment building in Kyiv on Wednesday. Genya Savilov / AFP via Getty Share Add NBC News to Google Oct. 14, 2026, 8:51 AM EDT By Abigail Williams , Dan De Luce , Gabe Gutierrez and Yuliya Talmazan Ukraine has accused Elon Musk’s SpaceX of disrupting its military operations by limiting Starlink internet services, as the country reeled from a pair of intense Russian missile attacks that it said came without the usual advance warning from allies. Facing pressure from President Donald Trump to halt strikes on Russia’s energy industry, Kyiv and its backers have worried Washington could cut off battlefield support to try and force it into concessions at the negotiating table. Ukrainian officials and their European partners were already scrambling to understand the status of U.S. intelligence sharing after the lack of alert ahead of two Russian ballistic missile strikes on Kyiv this week caused confusion, two Ukrainian and two European officials told NBC News. Trump insisted the U.S. was still sharing intel, but with relations spiraling Ukrainian officials and military units were on Wednesday accusing SpaceX of throttling a technology essential to their battlefield communications and drone operations. It was not immediately clear what might be behind the Starlink interruptions, though some Ukrainian officials said the timing could not be a coincidence given that Musk is a close Trump ally. Drone disruptions SpaceX had introduced speed limits on the operation of its Starlink satellite internet terminals overnight, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s defense tech adviser, Serhii Beskrestnov

Forget rockets — Longshot wants to fire cargo into space from a gun. See it at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026
items.d: Longshot is trying to build a gun big enough to make space data centers a reality.
items.fullText: Rockets are, infamously, a real pain in the butt. Our old friend physics forces rockets to be built with almost no room for error, and even then only a small fraction of their weight makes it to orbit. There are, at least in theory, other ways to do the job — space elevators, centrifuges, or a big chain hanging from a satellite in space and scooping up cargo from Earth. (Blue Origin spent some time thinking about that one before the idea wound up in a Neal Stephenson novel .) And then there’s an idea dating all the way back to Jules Verne: Use a big gun to shoot a projectile into space. Longshot Space Technology , a startup based in Alameda, California, is working on exactly that. The co-founders, CEO Mike Grace and CTO Nato Saichek, see an opportunity to take a technology that has already proven its worth and apply it to the pressing need for space launch. The startup has raised about $20 million from venture investors in service of its mission. When it comes to frontier technology, Grace says, “you can build something that has a lot of novelty, or you can do something really hard. You don’t get to do both.” He points to SpaceX as an example of a company that has “taken classically de-risked technology and scaled it aggressively.” What SpaceX did with NASA rocket research, he says, Longshot will do with multi-injection guns — designs that give a projectile extra boosts as it moves down the barrel — built for World War II and during 1960s research programs. The idea is to take all the work done by the first stage of a launch vehicle and collapse that into a reusable accelerator on the ground. Picture a steel pipe mounted horizontally over the ground, with tanks of high-pressure gas attached at ports spread across its length. SK하이닉스가 2013년 12월 세계 최초로 HBM을 상용화하는 과정에도 참여했다. 시상식은 오는 15일 대전 롯데시티호텔에서 열린다. 정지은 기자 jeong@hankyung.com 좋아요 싫어요 후속기사 원해요 ⓒ 한경닷컴, 무단전재 및 재배포 금지 한국경제 구독신청 한경 프리미엄9 구독신청 정지은 기자 한국경제신문 산업부에서 전자업계를 담당하고 있습니다. 제보 메일 환영합니다. items.fullText: NVIDIA Announces New Investments in France’s Startups Across all of Europe, NVIDIA has committed nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem. October 12, 2026 by Nat Ives 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! Companies in France are deploying agentic computing across industries spanning space, financial services, the public sector and scientific research, demonstrating how the country’s ecosystem has moved from ambition to application. France’s progress sits on deliberate groundwork. The AI Action Summit in February 2025 and Choose France Summits in 2025 and 2026 anchored major compute commitments on French soil. What the ecosystem has built since then spans the full stack. Read All NVIDIA in Europe Announcements NVIDIA’s Investments in France NVIDIA has been investing in France’s startup ecosystem, having previously invested in leading technology companies including Alice&Bob, Gradium and Scintil Photonics . Across all of Europe, NVIDIA has committed nearly $10 billion to the technology ecosystem. Today, NVIDIA announced new planned investments in Doctolib, Entalpic , Genesis AI and Pigment . These startups are innovating to solve challenges across healthcare, materials discovery, physical AI and business planning. Doctolib , a European healthcare technology company, builds agents that free up healthcare professionals to deliver better care, while providing patients with a digital health companion that improves access to care and supports more preventive, continuous medicine. Entalpic , a Paris-based startup, accelerates the engineering of advanced materials at the atomic scale, with particular expertise in surfaces and interfaces for semiconductor manufacturing and next-generation electronics. Genesis AI is a global robotics company developing general-purpose robots with frontier intelligence and capabilities through its foundation models, data collection systems, simulation infrastructure and robot hardware.
